newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Bekaert warns Belgian govt on job costs.
newsitem.headline: Bekaert warns Belgian govt on job costs.

text.p: Belgian steel wire and cord maker Bekaert NV warned on Thursday more companies could follow French carmaker Renault and close down factories in Belgium unless non-wage labour costs were slashed.

"I should like...to make a plea to the government to take urgent action to reduce the total burden of labour costs borne by companies in Belgium," chief executive officer Raf Decaluwe told a news conference on Bekaert's 1996 results.
Renault said last month it would close down its profitable Belgian plant in July to save money and rationalise production at its European factories.

Decaluwe cited an article written by a Belgian academic about the decision, which said that companies in Belgium which wanted to reduce costs had only four choices: move, replace people by machines, venture into the black economy or go bust.
"At Bekaert we are not prepared to leave it at those four choices. We are being forced by circumstances to open a debate on Belgium's high labour costs, Decaluwe said.
Bekaert profit in 1996 fell to 2.28 billion Belgian francs from 3.01 billion in 1995 as weak demand for its products, overcapacity in western Europe and cheap imports hit margins.
The net result included a 1.93 billion Belgian franc provision for a restructuring programme, the first phase of which is due to be completed by 1999.

Bekaert plans a second phase, mainly to reduce personnel in Belgium by around 350. It would start as soon as an agreement could be reached with unions, but could last longer than two years depending on the timescale for early retirements.
A first meeting with unions was held on Wednesday. Decaluwe hoped an agreement could be reached by the summer.
